Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

# AGENTS.md

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of
  adding compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current
  requirements. Avoid speculative abstractions, configuration, and
  indirection.
- Grow the system in layers. Start from the smallest version that works end
  to end, and add each new capability on top of a product that already
  works. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns clearly separated.
- Prefer established, well-maintained libraries when they reduce overall
  complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common
  functionality without a clear reason.
- Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own
  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.
- Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap
  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Terse by default: after an action, state what changed in three lines or
  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

- [Research scope: own commits only](research-scope-own-commits.md): consolidating "my research" means Steffen's commits and sessions, not teammates' branches
- [Shared working tree](shared-working-tree.md) — peer sessions commit in the same checkout; re-check git state, never leave temporary constant edits
- [Elicit worktree](elicit-worktree.md) — experiments live in ../ehlcodacabana-elicit on branch steffen/elicit (PR #14), not in the shared checkout

Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

content.content:
"""The model writes one paragraph of each e-mail: it answers the supplier's last e-mail like a
person would (its questions, its points, its situation). Code writes everything that binds or is
checked: figures, data IDs, the proposal. A paragraph with any digit, data ID or leak is dropped
and the template stands in. Hard timeout: the move goes out without the model if it is late."""

import logging
import os
import re
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
TIMEOUT_S = 15.0
MIN_S = 2.0  # less time than this left on the clocks: the template, no model call
# A late call is abandoned, not interrupted: it finishes in the background (httpx timeout) while
# the move goes out with the template.
POOL = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32, thread_name_prefix="writer")
FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\d|\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):|urgent|urgency|deadline|budget|no alternative|"
    r"walk away|other options|last chance|desperate|must close|time pressure|target price",
    re.I,
)

SYSTEM = """You are a senior buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, writing to a supplier.
Write ONLY the middle paragraph of our reply e-mail: 2 to 4 sentences, plain text, no greeting, no
sign-off, no lists.

In it:
- answer the supplier's last e-mail like a thoughtful person: respond to what it asked and to the
  reasons it gave, using only the facts listed under WHAT WE CAN SAY;
- acknowledge its situation where the notes give one (for example cash needs, full capacity, rising
  costs, a long relationship), sincerely and briefly;
- if it asks for something we cannot give, say so kindly and point to what we do offer;
- ask one short question only if QUESTION ALLOWED is yes.

Never write any number, price, percentage, date, quantity or data ID (code adds the figures). Never
mention urgency, deadlines, a budget, our alternatives or the lack of them, a target price, or that
we will walk away. Never invent facts, promises or commitments. Be polite, factual and warm unless the
tone says firm."""


def complete_from_env():
    """(system, user) -> text with the team's model over an OpenAI-compatible chat completions
    endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_EFFORT`), or None when not configured."""
    model, key = os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"), os.environ.get("LLM_API_KEY")
    if not model or not key:
        return None
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    client = httpx.Client(timeout=TIMEOUT_S, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})

    effort = os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT", "low")

    def complete(system, user):
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
        body = {"model": model, "messages": messages, "reasoning_effort": effort}
        r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


def paragraph(complete, brief, timeout=TIMEOUT_S):
    """The model's paragraph for this brief within `timeout` seconds of wall clock, or None (no
    model, no time, late, broken or unsafe)."""
    if complete is None:
        return None
    if timeout < MIN_S:
        log.warning("writer skipped: %.1fs left on the clocks", timeout)
        return None
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        text = (POOL.submit(complete, SYSTEM, brief).result(timeout=min(timeout, TIMEOUT_S)) or "").strip()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a slow or broken model must not cost the move
        log.warning("writer model failed after %.1fs: %s", time.monotonic() - t0, e)
        return None
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    if not text or len(text) > 900 or FORBIDDEN.search(text):
        log.warning("writer paragraph dropped: %r", text[:200])
        return None
    log.info("writer paragraph in %.1fs", time.monotonic() - t0)
    return text
"""E-mails from templates: every figure and ID comes from code, the wording stays polite and
factual. Never mentions urgency, a budget, our alternative's absence or our target."""

FIELDS = {
    "payment_days": lambda v: f"payment {v} days net",
    "contract_months": lambda v: f"{v} months" if v else "a single order",
    "volume_per_year": lambda v: f"{v} units a year",
    "lead_time_days": lambda v: f"lead time {v} days",
    "effective_date": lambda v: f"valid from {v}",
    "incoterm": lambda v: f"delivery {v}",
    "tooling_eur": lambda v: f"tooling EUR {v:.0f}" if v else "no tooling charge",
    "ppm_commitment": lambda v: f"{v} ppm",
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": lambda v: f"chargeback EUR {v:.0f} per complaint",
    "index_clause": lambda v: (
        f"price follows {v.get('series')} on {round((v.get('material_share') or 0) * 100)}% of the price, "
        f"deadband {v.get('deadband_pct') or 0}%"
        if v
        else "fixed price"
    ),
}


def describe(case, sheet):
    parts = [f"EUR {sheet['unit_price']:.2f} per unit"]
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        if field != "unit_price" and field in sheet and field in FIELDS:
            parts.append(FIELDS[field](sheet[field]))
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
    volume = sheet.get("volume_per_year") or fixed.get("volume_per_year") or case["buyer"]["need_per_year"]
    months = sheet.get("contract_months") or fixed.get("contract_months")
    span = f" over {months} months" if months else ""
    if "volume_per_year" not in case["negotiable"]:
        parts.append(f"for our full demand of {volume} units a year{span}")
    return ", ".join(parts)


# Sandbox D01, identical sheets, only the words varied: plain 50.00, firm 49.90, warm 49.60,
# asking what it needs 49.40 (docs/learnings.md). Asking invites the trade it wants.
ASK = "What would you need from us to move further on the price? We are open to discussing any term that helps you."


def email(case, sheets, claims, statements=(), first=False, moved=False, warm=True, paragraph=None):
    """The e-mail: our words (the model's paragraph, else the template's), then the code sentences
    that answer its asks (figures without IDs), the data arguments and the proposal exactly as code
    computed them."""
    lines = ["Dear Sir or Madam,", ""]
    if first:
        lines.append("Thank you for your offer and for the time your team has put into it.")
    elif moved:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply and for the step you have taken; we appreciate it.")
    else:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply.")
    if paragraph:
        lines.append(paragraph)
    elif warm:
        lines.append(
            "We value our cooperation and we understand the cost pressure on your side; we want an agreement "
            "that keeps our partnership healthy for both of us."
        )
    else:
        lines.append("We want an agreement that works for both sides.")
    if statements:
        lines.append("")
        lines += list(statements)
    if claims:
        lines.append("")
        lines += [c["text"] for c in claims]
    lines.append("")
    if len(sheets) == 1:
        lines.append(f"On this basis we propose: {describe(case, sheets[0])}.")
    else:
        lines.append("On this basis we propose one of these packages:")
        lines += [f"- Option {chr(65 + i)}: {describe(case, s)}" for i, s in enumerate(sheets)]
    if first and not paragraph:
        lines += ["", ASK]
    lines += ["", "Kind regards,", "Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


TRAITS = {
    "cash_need": "it is short of cash; when it gets paid matters a lot to it",
    "capacity_full": "it is fully booked; delivery time and a firm commitment matter to it",
    "spare_capacity": "it has free capacity and wants work for its machines",
    "price_frozen": "its management has frozen price cuts; other terms can move",
    "approval_2pct": "larger price steps need its pricing committee's approval",
    "deprioritising_us": "it focuses on customers with larger volumes",
    "hedged": "it bought its material forward at fixed prices",
    "open_book": "its owner once offered to walk us through its calculation",
    "stale_costing": "its costing has not followed the actual material prices",
    "partnership_2022": "it kept supplying at the old price during the 2022 crisis",
    "reference_customer": "it values having our company as a reference customer",
    "complains_late_pay": "it complained that our invoices were paid late",
}
OWNERS = {
    "family": "a family-owned company where the relationship matters",
    "group": "part of a larger group with formal approvals",
    "founder": "a small founder-run shop",
    "private": "a privately held company",
}


def brief(case, prof, last_body, facts, tone, question_allowed):
    """What the model needs for the paragraph: who the supplier is, what it wrote, what we may say."""
    who = OWNERS.get(prof.get("owner_type"), "a supplier")
    if prof.get("country") and prof.get("country") != "DE":
        who += f" based in {prof['country']}"
    traits = [TRAITS[s] for s in prof.get("signals", []) if s in TRAITS]
    out = [
        f"CASE: {case.get('title')} (we are the buyer; goal: {case['buyer'].get('category_goal')})",
        f"SUPPLIER: {who}." + (f" From our notes: {'; '.join(traits)}." if traits else ""),
        f"ITS LAST E-MAIL:\n{(last_body or '')[:1800]}",
        "WHAT WE CAN SAY:",
        *[f"- {f}" for f in facts],
        f"TONE: {tone}",
        f"QUESTION ALLOWED: {'yes' if question_allowed else 'no'}",
    ]
    return "\n".join(out)


def keepalive():
    return (
        "Dear Sir or Madam,\n\nthank you for your offer, which we are reviewing internally. Could you confirm "
        "how long it remains valid?\n\nKind regards,\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing"
    )
"""Which agent plays a case: `buyer` is our policy (`policy.py`, played by `runner.py`), `naive`
the kit's baseline."""

from arena_kit.agents import NaiveAgent
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

AGENTS = ("buyer", "naive")


def load_package(path):
    """The data package with its ID index built once, before parallel cases share it."""
    if not path:
        return None
    pkg = DataPackage(path)
    pkg.lookup("")
    return pkg


def naive_factory():
    return NaiveAgent
"""What the supplier's e-mail asks of us. The bots write their asks in a few fixed sentences
("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data.", "Faster payment would help us
more than anything"), so plain patterns read them; no model, no latency."""

import re

ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]

    model, key = os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"), os.environ.get("LLM_API_KEY")
    if not model or not key:
        return None
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    client = httpx.Client(timeout=TIMEOUT_S, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})

    effort = os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT", "low")

    def complete(system, user):
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
        body = {"model": model, "messages": messages, "reasoning_effort": effort}
        r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


def paragraph(complete, brief, timeout=TIMEOUT_S):
    """The model's paragraph for this brief within `timeout` seconds of wall clock, or None (no
    model, no time, late, broken or unsafe)."""
    if complete is None:
        return None
    if timeout < MIN_S:
        log.warning("writer skipped: %.1fs left on the clocks", timeout)
        return None
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        text = (POOL.submit(complete, SYSTEM, brief).result(timeout=min(timeout, TIMEOUT_S)) or "").strip()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a slow or broken model must not cost the move
        log.warning("writer model failed after %.1fs: %s", time.monotonic() - t0, e)
        return None
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    if not text or len(text) > 900 or FORBIDDEN.search(text):
        log.warning("writer paragraph dropped: %r", text[:200])
        return None
    log.info("writer paragraph in %.1fs", time.monotonic() - t0)
    return text
"""E-mails from templates: every figure and ID comes from code, the wording stays polite and
factual. Never mentions urgency, a budget, our alternative's absence or our target."""

FIELDS = {
    "payment_days": lambda v: f"payment {v} days net",
    "contract_months": lambda v: f"{v} months" if v else "a single order",
    "volume_per_year": lambda v: f"{v} units a year",
    "lead_time_days": lambda v: f"lead time {v} days",
    "effective_date": lambda v: f"valid from {v}",
    "incoterm": lambda v: f"delivery {v}",
    "tooling_eur": lambda v: f"tooling EUR {v:.0f}" if v else "no tooling charge",
    "ppm_commitment": lambda v: f"{v} ppm",
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": lambda v: f"chargeback EUR {v:.0f} per complaint",
    "index_clause": lambda v: (
        f"price follows {v.get('series')} on {round((v.get('material_share') or 0) * 100)}% of the price, "
        f"deadband {v.get('deadband_pct') or 0}%"
        if v
        else "fixed price"
    ),
}


def describe(case, sheet):
    parts = [f"EUR {sheet['unit_price']:.2f} per unit"]
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        if field != "unit_price" and field in sheet and field in FIELDS:
            parts.append(FIELDS[field](sheet[field]))
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
    volume = sheet.get("volume_per_year") or fixed.get("volume_per_year") or case["buyer"]["need_per_year"]
    months = sheet.get("contract_months") or fixed.get("contract_months")
    span = f" over {months} months" if months else ""
    if "volume_per_year" not in case["negotiable"]:
        parts.append(f"for our full demand of {volume} units a year{span}")
    return ", ".join(parts)


# Sandbox D01, identical sheets, only the words varied: plain 50.00, firm 49.90, warm 49.60,
# asking what it needs 49.40 (docs/learnings.md). Asking invites the trade it wants.
ASK = "What would you need from us to move further on the price? We are open to discussing any term that helps you."


def email(case, sheets, claims, statements=(), first=False, moved=False, warm=True, paragraph=None):
    """The e-mail: our words (the model's paragraph, else the template's), then the code sentences
    that answer its asks (figures without IDs), the data arguments and the proposal exactly as code
    computed them."""
    lines = ["Dear Sir or Madam,", ""]
    if first:
        lines.append("Thank you for your offer and for the time your team has put into it.")
    elif moved:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply and for the step you have taken; we appreciate it.")
    else:
        lines.append("Thank you for your reply.")
    if paragraph:
        lines.append(paragraph)
    elif warm:
        lines.append(
            "We value our cooperation and we understand the cost pressure on your side; we want an agreement "
            "that keeps our partnership healthy for both of us."
        )
    else:
        lines.append("We want an agreement that works for both sides.")
    if statements:
        lines.append("")
        lines += list(statements)
    if claims:
        lines.append("")
        lines += [c["text"] for c in claims]
    lines.append("")
    if len(sheets) == 1:
        lines.append(f"On this basis we propose: {describe(case, sheets[0])}.")
    else:
        lines.append("On this basis we propose one of these packages:")
        lines += [f"- Option {chr(65 + i)}: {describe(case, s)}" for i, s in enumerate(sheets)]
    if first and not paragraph:
        lines += ["", ASK]
    lines += ["", "Kind regards,", "Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


TRAITS = {
    "cash_need": "it is short of cash; when it gets paid matters a lot to it",
    "capacity_full": "it is fully booked; delivery time and a firm commitment matter to it",
    "spare_capacity": "it has free capacity and wants work for its machines",
    "price_frozen": "its management has frozen price cuts; other terms can move",
    "approval_2pct": "larger price steps need its pricing committee's approval",
    "deprioritising_us": "it focuses on customers with larger volumes",
    "hedged": "it bought its material forward at fixed prices",
    "open_book": "its owner once offered to walk us through its calculation",
    "stale_costing": "its costing has not followed the actual material prices",
    "partnership_2022": "it kept supplying at the old price during the 2022 crisis",
    "reference_customer": "it values having our company as a reference customer",
    "complains_late_pay": "it complained that our invoices were paid late",
}
OWNERS = {
    "family": "a family-owned company where the relationship matters",
    "group": "part of a larger group with formal approvals",
    "founder": "a small founder-run shop",
    "private": "a privately held company",
}


def brief(case, prof, last_body, facts, tone, question_allowed):
    """What the model needs for the paragraph: who the supplier is, what it wrote, what we may say."""
    who = OWNERS.get(prof.get("owner_type"), "a supplier")
    if prof.get("country") and prof.get("country") != "DE":
        who += f" based in {prof['country']}"
    traits = [TRAITS[s] for s in prof.get("signals", []) if s in TRAITS]
    out = [
        f"CASE: {case.get('title')} (we are the buyer; goal: {case['buyer'].get('category_goal')})",
        f"SUPPLIER: {who}." + (f" From our notes: {'; '.join(traits)}." if traits else ""),
        f"ITS LAST E-MAIL:\n{(last_body or '')[:1800]}",
        "WHAT WE CAN SAY:",
        *[f"- {f}" for f in facts],
        f"TONE: {tone}",
        f"QUESTION ALLOWED: {'yes' if question_allowed else 'no'}",
    ]
    return "\n".join(out)


def keepalive():
    return (
        "Dear Sir or Madam,\n\nthank you for your offer, which we are reviewing internally. Could you confirm "
        "how long it remains valid?\n\nKind regards,\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing"
    )
"""Which agent plays a case: `buyer` is our policy (`policy.py`, played by `runner.py`), `naive`
the kit's baseline."""

from arena_kit.agents import NaiveAgent
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

AGENTS = ("buyer", "naive")


def load_package(path):
    """The data package with its ID index built once, before parallel cases share it."""
    if not path:
        return None
    pkg = DataPackage(path)
    pkg.lookup("")
    return pkg


def naive_factory():
    return NaiveAgent
"""What the supplier's e-mail asks of us. The bots write their asks in a few fixed sentences
("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data.", "Faster payment would help us
more than anything"), so plain patterns read them; no model, no latency."""

import re

ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]

# Codacabana: Tacto Negotiation Arena

Team Codacabana at the European Hackathon League Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 October 2026,
Tacto track. Our AI buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier
bots and closes the deal with the lowest total cost, or walks away. Brief: `docs/challenge.md`.

## Setup

Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks   # secret scan, no pushes to main, Entire hooks
uv sync                               # the agent, Tacto's arena kit, pytest, ruff
cp .env.example .env                  # fill in the keys below
uv run arena data                     # data package into data/package
uv run arena me                       # the key works: team and practice quota
```

Environment variables (`.env.example`):

| Variable | What |
|---|---|
| `ARENA_URL` | `https://arena.tacto.ai` |
| `ARENA_API_KEY` | the team key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply |
| `ARENA_DATA` | `data/package` |
| `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | the model, any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint; optional `LLM_EFFORT` |

## Run

```sh
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                     # one sandbox case (free)
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10     # every hosted practice case (counts against the quota)
uv run buyer pull --set practice                  # finished sessions with trace -> logs/sessions/
uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v     # the Live Final: start before 12:00, leave it running
```

## Approach

Code owns every number: `buyer/policy.py` plans terms and prices with `total_cost`, cites data
by ID and refuses bad accepts; the model writes one paragraph of each e-mail (`buyer/llm.py`).
`buyer/runner.py` plays the cases. Design in `docs/design.md`, findings in `docs/learnings.md`.

## Develop

Rules for people and coding agents: `AGENTS.md`.

```sh
uv run pytest -q                 # our agent end to end against the local arena simulator
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format .
```
# Agent design

The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.

**Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
[how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Implemented (price engine)

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
   clamps them.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:

   ```
   supplier reply
     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
   ```

3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.

## Modules

| Module | Job | Run by |
|---|---|---|
| Runner | polls the final's case list, one coordinator per case, restarts after a crash | code |
| Coordinator | case brief, starts thread negotiators, shared state, decides when to close | code |
| Economics | C of any sheet, floor, anchor, target, concession steps, accept gate | code |
| Personas | one profile per supplier: traits with evidence, levers, history | model offline, code live |
| Claim bank | arguments as sentences with figure and data ID, computed as the arena checks them | code |
| Reader / writer | supplier e-mail to JSON; move to e-mail | small model, hard timeout |
| Fact check | supplier statements: confirmed, contradicted, selective, unverifiable (not built) | code |
| Guard | blocks leaks, unknown IDs, unplanned figures, broken must-haves | code |
| Fallback cascade | unknown supplier or part: case facts, data search, category averages, its documents | code |

## What feeds the brief, by impact

| # | Data | Decides | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | case file, quote PDF | C directly: need, horizon, rates, must-haves, alternative, options, standard terms | `GET /v1/cases`, `arena_kit.docs.standard_terms` |
| 2 | supplier cost floor | anchor, target, relationship charge | `should_cost`, cost-breakdown XLSX on request |
| 3 | index values of its cost drivers | justified price change, strongest claims | `cost_drivers`, `index_values`, `facts.json` |
| 4 | letters, notes, news | what moves it (cash, capacity, relationship), notice periods | `documents`, `correspondence/`, `news` |
| 5 | negotiation history | how far it usually moves | `negotiation_history` |
| 6 | intel, our invoices | archetype, payment lever | `supplier_intel`, `invoices`, `suppliers` (cash discount) |
| 7 | contracts and clauses | notice, index clauses, expiry, single sourcing | `contracts`, `contract_clauses`, `sourcing` |
| 8 | scorecards, QNs | quality lever | `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` |
| 9 | forecasts, PO prices, rival quotes | volume, price history, rival arguments | `forecast_lines`, `po_lines`, `quotes` |

The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are read at runtime.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:

- **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
- **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
  evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.

C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.

## Policy

A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
constants when the stance call times out:

| Constant | Values |
|---|---|
| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |

Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.

## Build order

1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
   fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
5. Persona reading and pacing.
6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.

## Generalise

- Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
  case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
- Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
- Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
  missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
- Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.

## Tactics

Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
before closing.

Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
attack on the arena: never.

# Agent design

The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.

**Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
[how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Implemented (price engine)

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
   and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
   clamps them.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:

   ```
   supplier reply
     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
     -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
     -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
     -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
   ```

3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.

## Modules

| Module | Job | Run by |
|---|---|---|
| Runner | polls the final's case list, one coordinator per case, restarts after a crash | code |
| Coordinator | case brief, starts thread negotiators, shared state, decides when to close | code |
| Economics | C of any sheet, floor, anchor, target, concession steps, accept gate | code |
| Personas | one profile per supplier: traits with evidence, levers, history | model offline, code live |
| Claim bank | arguments as sentences with figure and data ID, computed as the arena checks them | code |
| Reader / writer | supplier e-mail to JSON; move to e-mail | small model, hard timeout |
| Fact check | supplier statements: confirmed, contradicted, selective, unverifiable (not built) | code |
| Guard | blocks leaks, unknown IDs, unplanned figures, broken must-haves | code |
| Fallback cascade | unknown supplier or part: case facts, data search, category averages, its documents | code |

## What feeds the brief, by impact

| # | Data | Decides | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | case file, quote PDF | C directly: need, horizon, rates, must-haves, alternative, options, standard terms | `GET /v1/cases`, `arena_kit.docs.standard_terms` |
| 2 | supplier cost floor | anchor, target, relationship charge | `should_cost`, cost-breakdown XLSX on request |
| 3 | index values of its cost drivers | justified price change, strongest claims | `cost_drivers`, `index_values`, `facts.json` |
| 4 | letters, notes, news | what moves it (cash, capacity, relationship), notice periods | `documents`, `correspondence/`, `news` |
| 5 | negotiation history | how far it usually moves | `negotiation_history` |
| 6 | intel, our invoices | archetype, payment lever | `supplier_intel`, `invoices`, `suppliers` (cash discount) |
| 7 | contracts and clauses | notice, index clauses, expiry, single sourcing | `contracts`, `contract_clauses`, `sourcing` |
| 8 | scorecards, QNs | quality lever | `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` |
| 9 | forecasts, PO prices, rival quotes | volume, price history, rival arguments | `forecast_lines`, `po_lines`, `quotes` |

The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are read at runtime.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:

- **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
  quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
- **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
- **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
  evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.

C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.

## Policy

A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
constants when the stance call times out:

| Constant | Values |
|---|---|
| capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
| opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
| margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
| justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
| concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |

Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.

## Build order

1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
   fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
5. Persona reading and pacing.
6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.

## Generalise

- Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
  case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
- Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
- Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
  missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
- Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.

## Tactics

Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
before closing.

Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
attack on the arena: never.

What we know about the arena, its supplier bots and the data package, and what it means for the
agent. Basis, Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions covering all 10 hosted cases and 12
suppliers, 17 sandbox sessions, the team's simulator and sandbox experiments, and the data
package. Every euro figure and what-if score below was recomputed with `arena_kit.total_cost`. Evidence: `exports/` (every session, supplier thread,
e-mail and claim; schema in `exports/README.md`) and `analysis/explore.py` (the data package).

## Takeaways for the agent

1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
   (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
   engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
   D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
   49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
   supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
   acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
   price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
   answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
   asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
   to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
   (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing
   committee end much earlier: Nordmark walked away at 19 % (P02 v1), Ravensteiner gave its final
   offer in round 1 at a 15 % gap (P10 v1).
5. **Choose terms by C at the supplier's own valuation**, including a contract beyond our horizon
   (free for us, security for it) and the overtime a fully booked supplier charges for faster
   delivery (about 0.5 % of the price per day: Hrvelec, Ravensteiner). This alone moved P10 from
   a 42-day to a 56-day lead time.
6. **In relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.** D01: all claims at once pushed
   to 48.50 and scored 0.969; stopping near 48.90 scored 0.998, the relationship charge grows
   faster below.
7. **Only a supplier's standing sheet can be accepted** (an alternative returns 422). A better
   alternative is sent back as our sheet; it agrees and becomes standing (P10).
8. **Raw-material distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and refuse any deadband**
   (P08, P18): take their clause and negotiate the price; insisting on a deadband stalled them.
   But only when their sheet with the clause costs us less than their last one: Nordmark's copper
   clause came alone and cost 1.8 % of spend, score 0 (P02 `680eb11405186b42`,
   `d52ccdd3d2e07b3f`). That rule separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly.
9. **RFQ: the arena answers one call per session at a time** and each thread's 60 s clock runs
   from its reply, so sends are serialized by deadline; the cheapest rival offer is a new,
   verified claim to every other bidder every round (P05 0.83, D02 0.73).
10. **The ceiling is lower than 0.9.** Best per case over all teams averages 0.82 (`/v1/live`,
    Saturday evening); practice C_best for P04 needs 4.93 against a frozen 4.94.

## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)

- Records on P02 (0.85) and P08 (0.73) come from a lower round-1 counter, not from later rounds:
  our later rounds converge to the same price whatever the gap (P02 371.9 in v4 to v6).
- Three sheets of equal C for us in round 1 reveal what each lever is worth to the supplier
  (payment, lead time, ppm) and could lift P10 and P11.
- The close response of a final case carries `c_best`; calibrating anchors between waves from it
  is possible but needs a rules check first.
- Persona-specific wording beyond the generic paragraph (cash need, partnership 2022, reference
  customer) moves the round-1 counter.
- Prices fall much further when every sheet stays below the supplier's price and concessions
  are slow (house agent 0.75 on P08, ours 0.11 after agreeing in round 2).
- Cash-short suppliers give more price for 14 to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it
  costs us.
- Citing the best rival offer moves RFQ bidders; our probe never cited offers.
- Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.

# Learnings

What we know about the arena, its supplier bots and the data package, and what it means for the
agent. Basis, Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions covering all 10 hosted cases and 12
suppliers, 17 sandbox sessions, the team's simulator and sandbox experiments, and the data
package. Every euro figure and what-if score below was recomputed with `arena_kit.total_cost`. Evidence: `exports/` (every session, supplier thread,
e-mail and claim; schema in `exports/README.md`) and `analysis/explore.py` (the data package).

Add findings to the matching section, newest first: date, tag, the finding, its evidence (case,
session or data ID) and what it means for the agent. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the data package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under
Hypotheses. Correct or delete entries that turn out wrong.

## Takeaways for the agent

1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
   (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
   engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
   D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
   49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
   supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
   acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
   price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
   answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
   asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
   to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
   (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing
   committee end much earlier: Nordmark walked away at 19 % (P02 v1), Ravensteiner gave its final
   offer in round 1 at a 15 % gap (P10 v1).
5. **Choose terms by C at the supplier's own valuation**, including a contract beyond our horizon
   (free for us, security for it) and the overtime a fully booked supplier charges for faster
   delivery (about 0.5 % of the price per day: Hrvelec, Ravensteiner). This alone moved P10 from
   a 42-day to a 56-day lead time.
6. **In relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.** D01: all claims at once pushed
   to 48.50 and scored 0.969; stopping near 48.90 scored 0.998, the relationship charge grows
   faster below.
7. **Only a supplier's standing sheet can be accepted** (an alternative returns 422). A better
   alternative is sent back as our sheet; it agrees and becomes standing (P10).
8. **Raw-material distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and refuse any deadband**
   (P08, P18): take their clause and negotiate the price; insisting on a deadband stalled them.
   But only when their sheet with the clause costs us less than their last one: Nordmark's copper
   clause came alone and cost 1.8 % of spend, score 0 (P02 `680eb11405186b42`,
   `d52ccdd3d2e07b3f`). That rule separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly.
9. **RFQ: the arena answers one call per session at a time** and each thread's 60 s clock runs
   from its reply, so sends are serialized by deadline; the cheapest rival offer is a new,
   verified claim to every other bidder every round (P05 0.83, D02 0.73).
10. **The ceiling is lower than 0.9.** Best per case over all teams averages 0.82 (`/v1/live`,
    Saturday evening); practice C_best for P04 needs 4.93 against a frozen 4.94.

## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)

- Records on P02 (0.85) and P08 (0.73) come from a lower round-1 counter, not from later rounds:
  our later rounds converge to the same price whatever the gap (P02 371.9 in v4 to v6).

  (payment, lead time, ppm) and could lift P10 and P11.
